Accumulate gradients in shared memory first, then reduce and accumulate into global memory using atomics to avoid the >100x slowdown of naive adjoint-immediate implementations [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that a naive adjoint implementation (adjoint-immediate) which accumulates gradients directly in global memory using atomics is over 100x slower than the non-adjoint forward pass due to memory access conflicts. It further explains that the proposed solution, 'adjoint-delayed', involves accumulating gradients first in shared memory, then reducing them in parallel, and finally accumulating into global memory using atomics. This matches the claim's description of the method and the motivation (avoiding the >100x slowdown).
